text.p: --PaineWebber analyst Charles Olsziewski said Tuesday he planned to raise his 1997 and 1998 earnings estimates for Vivus, following the company's report Tuesday of first quarter earnings that were more than double the consensus forecast.
--Prior to the first quarter earnings report, Olsziewski had been forecasting earnings of $1 per share in fiscal 1997 and $2.15 in 1998. "Both numbers will be going up," he said.

--He cited strong earnings and sales from its Muse treatment for male impotence. He also said that at a conference call with analysts the company held on Tuesday, it refuted some of the recent rumors that have contributed to its stock's volatility.

--Olsziewski said he has a 12-month target price of $80 for Vivus stock. He said that 50 million men worldwide suffer from impotence and that Vivus could see strong growth by capturing just a small fraction of that market.

"I'm not saying they are going to have 50 percent market share. But if they get to 900,000 or a million customers, or two percent of the market by the year 2000, that would stll work out to earnings per share of $4.75."
--Olsziewski also noted the company plans to introduce a new and improved compound, that will correct impotence with fewer side effects than the current formulation.
